sahneler.metin: In 1906, one of Americas greatest cities burned for three straight days.
April eighteenth, twelve minutes past five in the morning.
The San Andreas fault slips, and the ground rolls like the sea.
But the earthquake is only the beginning of the nightmare.
Broken gas lines and toppled stoves start hundreds of fires.
The water mains have shattered, so there is nothing to fight them with.
The flames go on to destroy eighty percent of the city.
Three thousand people are gone, and a quarter million are homeless.
It was the fire, not the quake, that did most of the killing.
